newsitem.title: USA: FMC sees '97 growth, but moderating factors.
newsitem.headline: FMC sees '97 growth, but moderating factors.

text.p: FMC Corp, reporting record sales and income from continuing operations in 1996, said Tuesday it expects further growth in 1997, moderated by weakness in the soda ash and hydrogen peroxide markets.
Chairman Robert Burt, in a statement, also said that "startup expenses associated with our new herbicide and lithium plants" will affect 1997 performance.

FMC said sales of agricultural products continued to increase in the fourth quarter. However, earnings in the sector were lower than a year earlier due to spending and startup costs related to the planned introduction of Authority herbicide.

Continuing difficulties in the startup process at the company's new herbicide plant will result in a shortfall of quantities necessary to meet estimated demand in 1997, but it expects solid, year-over-year improvements in agricultural products performance.
It said startup of a new low-cost lithium plant in Argentina will be under way during the first half of 1997.
FMC today reported higher fourth quarter results.
